bank_plan.command: bank 65 byte group T0, fingers 66-84, CK_t/CK_c on 76/74
bank_plan.write: bank 64 byte groups T1 / T2 / T3, fingers 143-161 (the columns of the comb), WCK_c/WCK_t on 137/139 (CK0 pair, inverted)

stackup.required_fab_tolerance: finished thickness measured over the gold fingers 1.20 +/-0.10 mm (+/-8.3 %); a generic +/-10 % window (1.073..1.311 mm) is 0.027 / 0.011 mm outside the standard at the two ends, so the fab note must state the absolute tolerance
stackup.outer_copper_note: 0.035 mm is the nominal of the upstream table. The via-in-pad fill-and-cap plating (IPC-4761 type VII) can leave up to about 0.055 mm on F.Cu / B.Cu, fingers included: the card is then up to 0.04 mm thicker than the table
stackup.impedance_control: controlled impedance, fab may adjust widths by +/-0.02 mm: In3 0.15 mm 46 ohm; In3 pair 0.10 / 0.10 mm 85 ohm differential; F.Cu / B.Cu 0.20 mm 46 ohm; F.Cu / B.Cu pair 0.10 / 0.10 mm 92 ohm differential (WCK on B.Cu, RDQS on F.Cu; all +/-10 %). The outer values depend on the finished copper and mask (design/impedance_results.json, outer_copper_and_mask_cases): 0.20 mm = 46.7 / 45.6 / 44.8 ohm and the pair = 97.6 / 91.8 / 86.7 ohm for 0.035 Cu + 0.010 mask / 0.040 + 0.020 / 0.055 + 0.020
stackup.copper_finish: hard gold over nickel on the fingers (30 uin min), ENIG elsewhere
stackup.via_in_pad: filled and capped (IPC-4761 type VII) under U1 and at the ten command divider node vias (0.40 / 0.20, y = 5.85): their pads are 0.05 - 0.16 mm from 0201 solder lands. The ten node vias of the data side (DQ0-7, WCK_P / WCK_N, y = 6.00) are plain vias: their pads are 0.25 mm from the lands
stackup.edge: 0.25 mm x 45 deg chamfer only (no deep bevel); finger copper starts <= 0.30 mm from the edge

board.copper_to_edge_note: 0.15 only so that the finger pads pass; everything else keeps 0.30 mm from the outline (see floorplan.plane_plan.pull_back)
board.angles: 0/45/90/135 degrees only; rounded 90-degree arcs only inside tuning meanders

through_signal.use: signal vias outside U1 (divider nodes, read vias, finger vias) and every GND via inside the divider fields (command fence, shunt and capacitor GND vias)

through_power.use: supply vias and the GND vias of parts outside the divider fields

via_in_pad.use: under U1 only, filled and capped

rules.impedance_solver: scripts/impedance.py (2-D finite differences, er 4.29, prepreg 0.11, core 0.36, outer copper 0.040 and mask 0.020 as design values); results in design/impedance_results.json including the outer-layer corners 0.035 Cu + 0.010 mask and 0.055 Cu + 0.020 mask; accuracy about +/-5 %

bend_model.mitre: a mitred vertex is electrically shorter than its centre line by (k_mitre0 + k_mitre1 x w) x (angle turned, rad): 0.0201 mm per radian on the 0.15 mm trace (0.016 mm = 0.11 ps per 45-degree vertex), 0.0174 mm per radian on the 0.10 mm CK legs
bend_model.arc: an arc of centre radius r by (k_arc0 x w + k_arc1 x (r - r_lm)) x (angle turned, rad), r_lm = w / ln((r + w/2) / (r - w/2)): 0.021 / 0.023 / 0.029 mm per radian at r = 0.20 / 0.15 / 0.10 mm (0.036 mm = 0.25 ps per 90 degrees at the 0.15 mm used)
bend_model.legs: two adjacent antiparallel legs of one net lose 2 x k_leg x exp(-pi x gap / leg_decay_mm) x (their common length): gap = copper to copper; 1.9 % of the common length at 0.33 mm (leg pitch 0.48), 0.35 % at 0.57 mm (leg pitch 0.72, the one used)
bend_model.calibration: fitted to HFSS (2026 R1, lossless, er 4.29, 0.018 mm copper as PEC between two ground planes 0.488 mm apart, wave ports, adaptive at 8 GHz to delta S 0.002, phase of S21 at 0.5 .. 10 GHz against a straight line; the delay is flat over that band) runs of the tuning shapes of this board; results and residuals in DESIGN.md section 13 and design/ref/hfss_cmd_tuning.json. The model applies to every bend of an In3 trace: the tuning features, the 0.4 mm jogs into the balls, the CK split and the CK_P hook
bend_model.per_feature: the formula is local: bends that follow each other within about 0.2 mm interact. Each CA / CS net therefore carries the difference between an HFSS run of its own tuning feature and the formula (groups[CMD].tuning.per_net[net].hfss.residual_mm, at most 0.06 mm = 0.4 ps), added to the electrical length of that feature by the plan, the router and the gate
bend_model.used_by: scripts/tuning.py: build_netlist.py (targets, CK_P hook, tuning plan), scripts/pcb/s20_cmd.py (solver); scripts/data_side.py (every mitred vertex of the data side on any layer, the legs of the RDQS skew bump); scripts/pcb/check_pcb.py (gates 6 and 7 measure the board with it)

tuning.note: length is added with few, large bends: a parallel shift of the trace (two 45-degree runs, no 90-degree bend) and, where that is not enough, rounded bumps on the shifted run: legs 0.48 mm apart (gap 0.33 mm = 3.0 h, h = 0.11 mm to In2), centre radius >= 0.15 mm (the trace width), amplitude >= 0.30 mm (2 w). At least 0.33 mm (3 h) to the neighbouring trace everywhere. Shape per net: groups[CMD].tuning.per_net; delays are computed with rules.bend_model

CMD_SE.note: one trace per 0.8 mm BGA column channel; gap 0.65 mm = 4.3 w, Kb 0.2 %; matches the divider back impedance 68 || (91 + 39) = 44.6 ohm; 0.125 mm to the via pads of the channel (0.40 mm pads on 0.8 mm), hence class clearance 0.12 on In3. On the outer layers the class keeps 0.10 mm: the F.Cu escape of DQ7 passes row G (CA0 ball) in the 0.29 mm row channel, 0.10 mm from the ball lands

CMD_CK.uncoupled_note: the DRC adds up every layer: per leg 0.62 mm (node via to the pair) and 1.63 / 1.74 mm (split at row H) on In3, plus the two links of the divider column on the outer layers, 0.53 mm (series pad to node via) and 0.48 mm (node via to shunt pad): 3.26 / 3.37 mm. On In3 alone 2.25 / 2.37 mm, which scripts/pcb/check_pcb.py holds to 2.5 mm
CMD_CK.note: tightly coupled from the node vias to row G, centred on ball column 9 (via-in-pads of A9..G9 omitted): 0.45 mm to the via pads of columns 8 and 10. At row H the legs split around the H9 via (0.15 mm to the pads of H8 / H9 / H10): CK_N goes on to J9, CK_P hooks back into H9 from the north-east, which makes up the ball-row difference without a meander; per-leg back impedance 68 || (91 + 33) = 43.9 ohm

HOST_SE.note: 1.2 V side: finger to series resistor on the finger's own layer. Command stubs: 0.20 mm, straight lead-out past the row of finger vias (y = 3.05), then one 45-degree run onto the resistor pad. Stubs of the data side (write, WCK, RESET_n): 0.15 mm from the finger through the row of the finger vias (to y = 3.45: at 0.20 mm the stub of finger 161 would stand 0.075 mm from two V1P2 finger vias), 0.20 mm from there (floorplan.finger_stubs)

WR_DQ.note: ball to divider node without a via at the ball: 0.09 mm neck inside the land field of U1, 0.15 mm line on its level, one parallel 45-degree fan, tooth down the column axis into the node via = the T. Bundle pitch 0.55 mm (gap 0.40 mm = 3.6 h, h = 0.11 mm to In1), the upstream figure, wherever two lines run side by side outside the land field (0.566 mm between the fan diagonals, 0.80 mm between the teeth). max_width: the links series resistor - node via - shunt and the F.Cu read finger track of finger 215 are 0.20 mm; t_to_resistor_max_mm: copper from the node via to the land of the series resistor and of the shunt (the one on the far face through the barrel); divider_to_card_edge_max_mm: every land of the sixteen divider parts; write_plan_tolerance_ps: each net against its own planned total (the group is not matched on the card: groups[WR])

F.Cu.note: only the links of the two divider columns, as wide as those of the DQ columns

WR_WCK.skew_note: max_skew_mm is the DRC limit on the LENGTH difference of the nets WCK_P / WCK_N (vias included). There is no skew bump: WCK_N goes straight into its node via and WCK_P makes one 45-degree run of 1.0 mm to its own, which takes up the ball-row difference between E4 and D5. The electrical match (intra_pair_skew_ps, host included) is measured by gate 7 of scripts/pcb/check_pcb.py
WR_WCK.uncoupled_note: per leg about 0.35 mm at the balls and 1.4 / 1.0 mm at the split above the node vias, plus the two F.Cu links of each column (1.36 mm), which the DRC adds: held to max_uncoupled_mm; the board gate holds each B.Cu leg to max_uncoupled_b_cu_mm
WR_WCK.note: B.Cu pair from the via-in-pads of E4 / D5 on the one diagonal of via-free balls (D3 - C2 - B1), east as the lowest lane, south into its two divider columns; F.Cu only as the 0.20 mm links series resistor - node via - shunt of the two columns. The GND vias of the two shunts are mirror images about the axis of the B.Cu pair (0.55 mm on either side). f_cu_links_to_other_tracks_min: those links to the DQ4 tooth

RD_DQ.return_via_applies_to: every read via, both vias of the RDQS pair and the node vias of the outer columns (DQ4, DQ5, DQ1, DQ7)

node_return_via_exception.why: the node vias of the four inner columns stand at 0.8 mm pitch with the F.Cu tooth on the axis and the In3 riser in the lane between: a 0.40 mm via between two teeth would leave 0.125 mm to each (rule 0.27). Their return path is the shunt GND via south of the row (1.38 .. 2.04 mm) and the unbroken In1 / In2 / In4 planes (0.2 mm webs between the antipads). Accepted at this data rate (100 Mb/s target); widening the comb for it would lengthen every line

RD_DQ.note: the read branch of the nets DQ0-7. There is no part between the ball and the read finger, so line, divider node, read branch and read finger of a bit are ONE net, DQx, and KiCad has one class for it (WR_DQ); this entry holds the rules of the read branch and is written to the .kicad_dru for the layers the write class does not use (In3.Cu, B.Cu). In3 from the node via: one 45-degree run into the lane 0.40 mm east of the column, north to its level, east at 0.55 mm pitch (gap 0.40 mm = 3.6 h), one 45-degree ramp of the whole bundle, east to a via on its own level above the read finger; from that via straight down to the finger on the finger's own outer layer, 0.20 mm. in3_gap_drc: the DRC value leaves 0.01 mm for the rounding of the ramp vertices; the board gate holds in3_gap_min. in3_to_foreign_via_pad_min: the upstream figure is 0.275 (the DQ6 line past the DQ7 node via). return_via_max_mm: a GND via within this distance of every via named in return_via_applies_to, return_via_min_mm centre to centre (0.15 mm between the pads); node_return_via_exception: the four inner node vias. read_plan_tolerance_ps: each net against its own planned total (the read group is not matched on the card: groups[RD_P]); read_end_crossings_max: no read finger track crosses an In3 read line of another bit (the fingers are taken in the order of the bundle)

RD_RDQS.uncoupled_note: what the DRC adds up per leg: the ball end (C4 lies one row beyond B3), the skew bump of RDQS_P (RDQS_N runs alone past it), the split to the two vias of the pair and the 0.40 mm link to the 150 ohm load
RD_RDQS.note: RDQS_P / RDQS_N: In3 pair from the via-in-pads of B3 / C4 through the row channel B|C, east between the two lower and the six upper F.Cu lines, on ONE 45-degree run to the north-east across the six diagonals of the F.Cu fan (90 degrees to them), east above every read via, on ONE 45-degree run of 3.0 mm down to the axis of the host pair DQS6 and south to one via pair just above fingers 219 / 221 (y = 8.50, the lowest a through via can stand: 0.90 mm from the VREF_RD bus on B.Cu), like the eight read DQ lines; then 5.8 mm of F.Cu straight down into the fingers, 1.075 mm EAST of the last read finger track (finger 215): the pair crosses no read line. The two 150 ohm loads stand beside the coupled pair on 0.40 mm links in the row of the 39 ohm resistors, on F.Cu like the pair, GND on the finger vias of the VSS pairs 217 / 218 and 222 / 223. One skew bump on RDQS_P, on In3 beside U1, where the skew arises. No series part, one net per leg. match_to_dq_ps: none, the read group is not matched on the card and the strobe is not matched to it; plan_tolerance_ps: each leg against its own planned total; the offset of the strobe from the centre of the read group is in groups[RD_RDQS] and in design/gateware_deskew.json; pair_to_read_via_min: the pair past the pad of a read via or of a return via; bump_leg_gap_min: 3 h

VREF.note: VREF_Nx: finger to 39 ohm, at most 5 mm; never routed across the card. 0.20 mm to everything, 0.90 mm from a VREF track to any track or via of a switching class on the same layer. Three places bend that, each with its own rule: the two lands of an 0201 are 0.18 mm apart (land_clearance_0201); the N stub of finger 211 passes the finger via of 209 / 210 and the tie of 213 at 0.14 mm (finger_via_row_clearance, rule area finger_via_row); the bus changes side between the read tracks of fingers 212 and 215 (keep_from_switching_nets_east_end, rule area vref_east_end: 0.405 mm as built, the track of 212 displaced 0.235 mm west and that of 215 0.175 mm east of their finger axes for it)

POWER.note: pours and planes; tracks at least 0.25 mm (the finger-to-via ties; 0.20 mm inside the BGA field), 0.30 mm and more elsewhere

rules.pair_naming: KiCad recognises a differential pair only by the suffixes _P / _N (or + / -) at the end of the net name. The three pairs are therefore named CK_P / CK_N, WCK_P / WCK_N and RDQS_P / RDQS_N (_P = JEDEC _t, _N = JEDEC _c) and their finger-side nets CK_F_P / CK_F_N and WCK_F_P / WCK_F_N (RDQS has no finger-side net: no series part), so that the pair router, the diff_pair_gap / diff_pair_uncoupled / skew constraints and the pair tuner work. WCK1_T / WCK1_C (unused byte, static) are not a routed pair and keep their names

groups.name: CMD
groups.layer: In3.Cu (between In2 GND and In4 GND); finger-side stubs on the finger's own outer layer
groups.match: delay from the FPGA die pad to the U1 ball (host copper + FPGA package + card)

tuning.where: In3, in the straight run between the fence vias (y = 7.50) and row A of U1 (y = 12.00): the 45-degree runs of the shifts leave the channel axis at y = 7.80 and rejoin it at y = 11.70; the copper of the bump legs stays inside y 7.90 .. 11.60
tuning.meander: few, large bends (rules.bend_model): every net runs parallel to its channel axis, shifted away from the CK corridor between two 45-degree runs (the west half fans out to the west, the east half to the east); nets that need more add rounded bumps on the shifted run, all pointing east, legs 0.72 mm apart (gap 0.33 mm = 3.0 h) on the common rows y = 8.67 + k x 0.72, corner radius >= 0.15 mm, amplitude >= 0.30 mm; >= 0.33 mm (3 h) to the neighbouring trace. No bump faces the CK pair closer than the pair rule
tuning.delay_model: trims are electrical: centre line less the bend corrections of rules.bend_model
tuning.ck: the CK pair is not meandered. It is the longest path of the group and sets the total. The row difference between H9 and J9 is made up by the hook of CK_P (floorplan.command.ck_split)

groups.note: card delay = copper from the finger top (y = 2.70) to the ball, vias by height between the middles of the copper layers, both sides of the series resistor counted, In3 bends by their electrical length (rules.bend_model); no common offset is used: the board is tuned to these targets; the host + package figures are good to about +/-5 ps, so the residual is removed per bit with ODELAY; no tuning inside the BGA field

groups.name: WR
groups.layer: F.Cu (microstrip over In1 GND), no via at the ball; the series resistor on the finger's face
groups.match: NOT matched on the card. Delay from the FPGA die pad to the U1 ball (write finger, series resistor, node via, tooth, line, neck) as it falls in the comb; the per-bit output delay of the FPGA closes it (deskew)
groups.tolerance_of: each net against its own planned total (per_net_planned_total_ps), not against a common target

deskew.status: accepted by the user ("The write group's spread is acceptable")
deskew.method: per-bit output delay in the FPGA (ODELAYE3 of the HP bank, DELAY_FORMAT = TIME): each bit is delayed by the latest total of the group minus its own total, so that all eight arrive with the latest one
deskew.file: design/gateware_deskew.json (written by gate 7 of scripts/pcb/check_pcb.py from the delays measured on the board)
deskew.why_not_on_the_card: a comb on one layer is planar for one order only (the lowest line takes the westmost column), and the corner escape puts the two balls with the longest necks (E6, F5) on the two top lines, which also get the two farthest columns. Finger choice moves about 8 ps (bank 64 hosts span 602 .. 615 ps). Closing it to +/-10 ps on the card needs about 20 mm of serpentine on six nets, three of which are interior lines at 0.40 mm gap from ball to node with no room for it

tuning.method: none: the group is planned as it falls (no serpentine, no trim feature); see deskew
tuning.bend_model: rules.bend_model applied to every mitred vertex of the path on F.Cu / B.Cu as an estimate (0.46 .. 1.01 ps per net)

groups.note: card delay = finger top (y = 2.70) -> stub -> series resistor (0.64 mm) -> node via (barrel between the middles of the copper layers: none for a front finger, the whole board for a back finger) -> tooth -> line -> neck -> ball. The totals span 748.0 .. 801.5 ps (centre 774.8, +/-26.7): +/-26.7 ps is 0.27 % of the 10 ns unit interval at 100 Mb/s, and the write timing is trained per bit in the gateware anyway (tWCK2DQI 300 .. 900 ps)

groups.name: WR_WCK
groups.layer: B.Cu (microstrip pair over In4 GND) between the via-in-pads of E4 / D5 and the node vias; F.Cu only inside the two divider columns (series resistor, node via, shunt in line)
groups.match: P to N only; WCK is not matched to DQ (tWCK2DQI is 300..900 ps: write timing is trained in gateware)
groups.polarity: WCK_P (= WCK_t, ball E4) is on finger 139, the N pin of the host pair (AG18); WCK_N (= WCK_c, ball D5) on finger 137, the P pin (AF18): the gateware drives the pair inverted. Reason: the B.Cu pair turns south into its two divider columns with the E4 leg on the east
groups.note: no skew bump: the two legs end differently (WCK_N straight into its node via, WCK_P on one 45-degree run of 1.0 mm), which takes up the ball-row difference between E4 and D5 to -0.54 ps with the host. Both legs pass the same two barrels and the same 0.20 mm links

groups.name: RD_P
groups.layer: F.Cu line and tooth (shared with WR) + node via + In3 branch from the node via to the read via (In3 between In2 GND and In4 GND) + the read finger's own outer layer from that via down to the finger; one net per bit
groups.match: NOT matched on the card. Delay from the U1 ball to the FPGA die pad (line + branch + host copper + FPGA package, bends by rules.bend_model) as it falls with the read fingers taken in the order of the In3 bundle (no read-end crossing); the per-bit input delay of the FPGA closes it (deskew)
groups.tolerance_of: each net against its own planned total (per_net_planned_total_ps), not against a common target

deskew.status: accepted by the user ("Same with read group"): built as the read end without crossings
deskew.method: per-bit input delay in the FPGA (IDELAYE3 of the HP bank, DELAY_FORMAT = TIME, DELAY_VALUE in ps; range 0 .. 1100 ps, 512 taps of 2.1 .. 12 ps): each bit is delayed by the latest total of the group minus its own total, so that all eight arrive at the capture flops with the latest one
deskew.file: design/gateware_deskew.json (written by gate 7 of scripts/pcb/check_pcb.py from the delays measured on the board)
deskew.why_not_on_the_card: the user asked for fewer crossings between layers and allowed the DQ order to change in the gateware. With the In3 lines in the order of the comb (fixed) the read fingers can be taken so that no finger track crosses an In3 line of another bit in exactly one order: the lowest line (the east column, DQ7) ends first, on the westmost finger. That order makes the short lines shorter and the long ones longer, and no level set helps (a raised line takes the lines above it with it, and the late lines are the top ones): +/-56.8 ps. Matching it on the card takes 20 read-end crossings (the comb as built before: +/-9.7 ps)

tuning.method: none: no serpentine, no raised level. The read vias stand on a regular staircase, 0.55 mm per line from y = 8.20 up in the order of the bundle (1 mm of level would be 8.93 ps); see deskew
tuning.assignment: the eight admissible P / N pairs of bank 66 (182 .. 215) taken west -> east by the In3 lines bottom -> top: the only assignment without a read-end crossing (floorplan.data.read_end_choice)

groups.note: card delay = ball -> neck -> line -> tooth -> node via (F.Cu to In3) -> In3 branch -> read via (In3 to the finger's face) -> finger track -> read finger top (y = 2.70); barrels between the middles of the copper layers; every mitred vertex by rules.bend_model. The totals span 836.0 .. 949.7 ps (centre 892.8, +/-56.8): the per-bit input delays are 0 .. 113.7 ps, a tenth of the IDELAY range; the host figures in them are good to about +/-5 ps, so read training refines them

groups.name: RD_RDQS
groups.layer: In3 (pair between In2 GND and In4 GND) from the via-in-pads of B3 / C4 to the via pair just above the fingers, F.Cu (microstrip pair over In1 GND) for the last 5.80 mm into fingers 219 / 221; no series part

NOT matched to the read DQ group (which is not matched on the card): each leg is held to its own planned total; the pair stays on In3 to a via pair just above its fingers (like the read DQ lines) and arrives +30.3 ps from the centre of the read group, a figure of the deskew table

in3_pad_trim.why: the via-in-pads of C4 / B3 (RDQS_N / RDQS_P) connect on In3 and keep a pad there; the pad of C4 stands beside the CA0 trace. With the 0.40 mm pad of every other via-in-pad it would be 0.125 mm from the trace and couple RDQS_N into CA0 at 1.15 % of the RDQS swing for the fastest edge (HFSS, design/ref/hfss_ca0_data_corner.json); at 0.35 mm (annular ring 0.10 mm, the board minimum) it is 0.15 mm away and couples 0.95 %. B3 is trimmed with it (one pad size for the pair)

via_in_pad.finish: filled and capped (IPC-4761 type VII), flat for the ball on F.Cu and for the 0402 / 0201 pads that sit on them on B.Cu
via_in_pad.unused_inner_pads_note: no pad on an inner layer on which the via connects to nothing (F.Cu and B.Cu keep theirs). On In3 the command traces then pass the barrels of the neighbouring ball columns at 0.25 mm (hole clearance 0.20) instead of their pads at 0.125 mm, and the antipads in the GND planes shrink from 0.60 to 0.55 mm (0.25 mm of plane between two ball columns)

b_cu_ties.note: CK_c_B has no VDDQ neighbour: its via-in-pad is tied on B.Cu to the VDDQ via of T4

unused_byte.removed: RN401 / RN402 (2 x 4 x 10 k) with their eight F.Cu escapes west out of the ball field and two GND vias: the escapes crossed the In3 command bundle 15 times in plan view

floorplan.finger_stub_rule: every track that leaves a signal finger starts 0.10 mm inside the finger pad (y = 2.60) and is drawn exactly as listed in finger_stubs. Command stubs: straight up the lead-out line, then one 45-degree run that ends on the centre of pad 1 of the series resistor. Stubs of the data side (floorplan.data.wires): write, WCK and RESET_n 0.15 mm ('neck') up to y = 3.45, above the pads of the finger vias, 0.20 mm ('wide') from there, one 45-degree run onto the pad; read tracks 0.20 mm straight north to the read via (a 0.175 mm step in the finger-via row where a finger via stands beside them); the RDQS legs run straight into fingers 219 / 221; reference stubs straight up the finger axis
floorplan.finger_via_rule: one 0.40 / 0.20 through via at y = 3.05 for every VSS / VDD finger pair (and for the single VDD finger 163), tied to each finger of the pair with a 0.25 mm track on that finger's own layer. Position: axis of the back finger, else axis of the front finger, else the middle of the pair (the first that keeps 0.15 mm from every planned finger track; 0.20 mm to a reference stub is accepted where nothing better exists). Placed by s10_escape together with the field vias

command.description: ten 0201 divider columns on the 0.8 mm pitch of the BGA column channels; series resistor on the finger's own side below the node via, shunt on the opposite side above it. command.ck: CK_N / CK_P node vias at x 19.525 / 20.325 converge at once into a 0.10 / 0.10 pair centred on x = 19.925 (no fence via on that line); the via-in-pads of A9..G9 are omitted (U1.via_in_pad) so the pair has a 1.2 mm via-free corridor. 0.75 mm below row H the legs split into the two column channels beside the H9 via: CK_N goes on to J9, CK_P passes H9 on the east and hooks back into it

data.description: the data side as one plan (scripts/data_side.py, DESIGN.md section 14): 'T at the divider', comb form. Per DQ: ball - 0.09 mm neck - F.Cu line on its level - one parallel 45-degree fan - tooth down the column axis into the node via (y = 6.00) = the T. At the T: 240 ohm in line on the finger's face and 150 ohm back to back on the other face (lands 0.25 mm from the via pad), the shunt GND via south of the row. The read branch leaves the node via on In3: one 45-degree run into the lane 0.40 mm east of the column, north to its level, east in an ordered bundle at 0.55 mm pitch, one 45-degree ramp, a via on its own level above its read finger, finger track straight down; the read fingers are taken in the order of the bundle (lowest line, westmost finger), so no finger track crosses an In3 line and the read vias form a regular staircase. WCK on B.Cu (lowest lane). RDQS on In3, then F.Cu down into the host pair DQS6 east of every read finger. Neither group is matched on the card (design/gateware_deskew.json). Reference networks in two rows with the bus at the north end

outer_layer_ground.policy: NO ground flood and no copper thieving on F.Cu / B.Cu, and no stitching grid: as on the upstream board (GND zones there: 4 % of F.Cu, 3 % of B.Cu, two local pours at its regulators), the outer layers carry tracks, pads and a few local POWER pours. outer_layer_ground.gnd_pads: every GND pad of every part reaches In1 / In2 / In4 through a via of its own net: in the pad (U1 balls, exposed pads of U2 / U4 / U5), or through a track of at most 1.5 mm on its own layer (VSS fingers: the tie to the finger via of their pair; two-pad parts: a stub to a via beside the pad, which two neighbours may share). Counted pad by pad on the board by gate 9
outer_layer_ground.gnd_vias: a GND via stands only where it serves a GND pad or the return current of a layer change (fence vias of the command field, return vias of the read vias and of the RDQS via pair): none exists to tie an outer pour to the planes
outer_layer_ground.local_gnd_pours_note: none: the three regulators are small linear regulators whose exposed pads carry their own vias; the upstream board uses local GND pours only around its switching regulators

open_end.answer: not bad. Worst corner (driver 30 % stronger than nominal at the 40 ohm setting): 0.539 V / -0.122 V at the pin, 1.6 ns per edge outside the single-ended window of the MIPI HS receiver (-0.04 .. 0.46 V), far inside the recommended range of the pin (-0.20 .. 1.40 V). Nominal driver: 0.445 V / -0.056 V, 0.29 ns below the window after a falling edge, never above it. In every corner the pin is within 30 mV of its final level 5 ns after the edge arrives and within 20 mV after 8 ns: the ringing is over long before a mid- or late-UI sample at 100 Mb/s (10 ns). The 22 ohm resistors kept the pin inside the window in all corners (0.429 V / -0.012 V at worst); what is given up is that margin for 1 .. 2 ns after each edge
open_end.gateware_knobs: the same damping is available without parts: MR3 OP[2:0] (pull-down drive strength 48 or 60 ohm instead of 40) and the SoC-ODT / pull-up calibration code of MR17. 60 ohm keeps a strong driver at 0.433 V / -0.048 V; a nominal 48 ohm driver stays inside the window (0.399 V / -0.027 V). The price is read level (150 / (150 + R))
